title: Infinitely many elliptic curves with torsion Z/2Z × Z/4Z and rank at least six
abstract: A Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of the paper "Infinitely many elliptic curves with torsion Z/2Z × Z/4Z and rank at least six" by Manvir Jaswal. Theorem 1.1 says that infinitely many elliptic curves over Q have torsion subgroup Z/2Z × Z/4Z and rank at least six, with infinitely many distinct j-invariants. The curves are fibers of a one-parameter family of Dujella and Peral, y² = x(x + a²)(x + b²), which has rank three over Q(m) and gains three further independent points over the function field of a curve C of genus one; congruences carry the independence of the six points, and the torsion, from one rational point of C to infinitely many. Theorem 1.2 shows that the smooth projective model of C is isomorphic over Q to an elliptic curve of conductor 9240 and rank one, that the family has rank exactly six over Q(C), and that at all but finitely many rational points of C its fibers have torsion exactly Z/2Z × Z/4Z and rank at least six. Theorem 8.1 gives a second such family, over a curve of genus one whose Jacobian has rank two. All 19 numbered results of the paper are proved. The theorems take published theorems of other authors as hypotheses, each stated in general form, about no curve or surface of the paper; Theorem 1.1 takes four: Mazur's torsion theorem, the integrality of torsion points at odd primes, that reduction at a prime of good reduction is a homomorphism, and that the points of an elliptic curve over Q_p form a compact topological group. Comparator checks Theorem 1.1; the other results are proved in the same library.
